- TPS2116 (TI SLVSFG1A, sec 6.1): VIN1/VIN2, VOUT and MODE absolute maximum is -0.3 to 6 V; recommended maximum is 5.5 V. The datasheet gives no hot-plug or input-transient guidance.
- TP4056: VCC absolute maximum is 8 V. The quoted "Adding a 1.5 ohm resistor in series with a ceramic capacitor will minimize start-up voltage transients" is verbatim at lcsc_C16581.txt lines 1214-1222.
- SMF6.5CA: VBR 7.22-7.98 V at 10 mA, Vc 11.2 V at 17.9 A.
- Littelfuse 0805L100: Rmin 0.060, R1max 0.210. Brightking SMD0805B100TFT: Rmin 0.040, R1max 0.230.
- CR1 therefore cannot hold USB_VBUS below 6 V. That is a plain datasheet fact.

**Physics (wf/verify/vbushp_nl.cir)**
I built my own LTspice deck. It differs from the finder's in three ways: C2 is a nonlinear X5R model (Q = 10u*4.5*atan(V/4.5), about 4.5 uF at 5 V and 2.9 uF at 7 V), the 21 mOhm pre-fuse track is a separate element, and the tracks to U2 and C2 are separate branches. Source is 5.25 V with 50 mOhm.

| Type-C-limit cable, 0.25 ohm / 0.6 uH | 0.12 ohm | 5.43 V | none |
| Type-C-limit cable, 0.25 ohm / 0.6 uH | 0.06 ohm | 5.66 V | none |
| Good 1 m 20 AWG cable, 0.13 ohm / 0.6 uH | 0.12 ohm | 6.04 V | about 1 us |

verify:reproduce:vbus-hotplug-overshoot-.corrections:
All refs, nets, coordinates and datasheet numbers in the claim are correct. My corrections concern how likely the worst cases are.

1. **PTC minimum resistance overstates the worst case.**
   - The top-of-range peaks (7.2-7.4 V) assume F1 at Rmin, 0.04 or 0.06 ohm. Both PTC datasheets define Rmin as the un-soldered initial state.
   - After reflow the resistance is higher, typically about 0.1-0.2 ohm, bounded by R1max of 0.21 or 0.23 ohm.
   - The 0.15-0.2 V difference between the JLC build (Brightking) and the hand build (Littelfuse) is therefore mostly academic.

2. **The excursion depends on the cable.**
   - A cable at the Type-C IR-drop limit (0.25 ohm round-trip) peaks at 5.4-5.7 V, so there is no violation.
   - Low-resistance cables (about 0.2 ohm or less, such as 1-2 m of 20 AWG) reach 6.0-6.6 V with F1 at 0.06-0.12 ohm, and about 7.1 V for 2 m of 20 AWG with F1 at 0.07 ohm.
   - Time above 6 V is about 1-5 us.
   - Short 0.3 m cables are benign (5.4-6.1 V) because inductance falls along with resistance.
   - A PC port with a 0.1 ohm power switch gives about 5.3 V.

3. **A nonlinear X5R model for C2 makes the peak slightly worse than the finder's linear 4 uF model.**
   - The extreme corner is 7.86 V nonlinear versus 7.08 V linear.
   - In that corner CR1 starts to conduct (about 4 mA), so "TVS never reaches breakdown" holds in every case except that one.

4. **The title singles out CR1, but the limitation is generic.** Any 5 V-standoff TVS has VBR of 6.4 V or more. The real issue is undamped ceramic on a hot-pluggable input feeding a part with a 6 V absolute maximum (TPS2116 VIN1 and MODE). The TP4056 (8 V) is not at risk in realistic cases.

5. **The 5.25 V source is the top of the vSafe5V range.** Most chargers idle at 5.0-5.15 V, which scales the peaks down by about 2-4%.

6. **The recommendation is sound and I verified it.** With 1 ohm in series with C2, the peak is 5.25-5.28 V in every simulated case; C25 stays undamped and the series C2 branch acts as the snubber. No board change is needed before ordering. Scope USB_VBUS on the first article, and if a fix is needed, replacing C2 with a 0603 resistor plus a relocated capacitor is a cheap rework.
